conflicts.subject: federated-email-join
conflicts.detail: B ignores email_verified; joining a federated sign-in to a password account by an unverified email would let anyone who controls a provider account claim another person's account
solutions: Join only when the provider says the email is verified; otherwise create a separate account
Never join automatically; require the user to link from a signed-in session
conflicts.recommended: Join only when email_verified is true; otherwise a separate account (the user's decision)

resolution.decision: A federated sign-in joins an existing account only when the provider says the email is verified (email_verified is True); otherwise it creates a separate account, and an unverified email never takes ownership of an address

conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User primary keys differ (A: integer, B: text)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: One User entity with opaque string ids (random uuid4 hex) for every account; A's integer ids and B's 'lu-<n>' ids kept in legacy_id if data is ever imported

conflicts.subject: provider
conflicts.detail: Identity providers differ (A: local; B: external oauth provider (google-style))
solutions: Choose one identity provider and migrate accounts to it
Link accounts by verified email during migration
conflicts.recommended: One identity system for the unified app

resolution.decision: One identity system: local password provider plus external OAuth providers, all resolving to one User through an Identity table keyed by (provider, subject)

conflicts.subject: model
conflicts.detail: Authorization models differ (A: one role string per user, no permission checks in this app; B: one role string per account, no permission checks in this app; C: rbac: role -> permission set)
solutions: Choose one authorization model and express the others' rules in it
conflicts.recommended: One authorization model with one permission check function

resolution.decision: C's RBAC (role -> permission set) is the one authorization model; A's and B's unchecked role strings are mapped into it

conflicts.subject: default_role
solutions: Choose one value and record why
Make it a setting if both are legitimate
conflicts.recommended: Pick one value with the user; make it configurable only if both are needed

resolution.decision: Password registration gets editor (A user -> editor); new OAuth accounts get viewer (B member -> viewer); a joined account keeps its existing role

conflicts.subject: duplicate-registration
conflicts.detail: A overwrites an existing account when the same email registers again (account takeover)
solutions: Reject a duplicate email with an error
Keep A's overwrite
conflicts.recommended: Reject duplicates; one account per email

resolution.decision: Reject a duplicate email (case-insensitive) with an error instead of overwriting the account

conflicts.subject: role-change-actor
conflicts.detail: C's set_role trusts a caller-supplied actor role, does not validate the new role and has no rule against raising your own role
solutions: Resolve the actor from the session token, validate the role, refuse raising your own role
Keep C's behaviour
conflicts.recommended: Actor from session; only admins; role must exist; nobody raises their own role (user decision)

resolution.decision: set_role resolves the caller from the session token; only admins (manage_roles) may change roles; the role must be viewer/editor/admin; nobody can raise their own role
resolution.note: admin-only and no self-raise are user decisions in task.md; actor-from-session and role validation pre-approved by the benchmark operator

conflicts.subject: roles
conflicts.detail: Role sets differ (A: user; B: member; C: admin, editor, viewer)
solutions: Map every source role to a unified role set and write the mapping down
Model special powers (such as approving) as permissions, not extra roles
conflicts.recommended: One role set plus explicit permissions; map every source role

resolution.decision: Unified roles viewer, editor, admin; mapping A user -> editor, B member -> viewer, C roles unchanged; any other source role raises KeyError

conflicts.subject: user.id
conflicts.detail: User.id types differ (A: integer, B: text)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: User.id is text (uuid4 hex) for all accounts; integer A ids widen to text in legacy_id

conflicts.subject: methods
conflicts.detail: Sign-in methods differ (A: password; B: oauth)
solutions: Offer the union of kept sign-in methods through one identity system
Drop sign-in methods no kept feature needs
conflicts.recommended: One identity system that offers the sign-in methods kept features need

resolution.decision: Offer both password and OAuth sign-in through the one identity system

conflicts.subject: user
conflicts.detail: User exists in A:User, B:Account; fields not shared: hash (only A), provider (only B), salt (only A), subject (only B)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge A:User and B:Account into one User entity; B's provider and subject move to an Identity entity linked to User
